root_cause: RTL defect DIS-20 (per verification_plan.yaml lines 1404-1415): rtl.sv lines 45-48 hardwire the open-drain drive controls `assign sda_oe = 1'b1; assign scl_oe = 1'b1; assign sda_out = 1'b0; assign scl_out = 1'b0;`. The controller therefore always actively drives SDA/SCL low and never releases them. Because the frozen TB models the bus as open-drain with an external pull-up (i2c_pins.py resolve_sda_level/resolve_scl_level: oe==0 => pull-up high, oe==1 => driven value), every idle cycle resolves SDA to 0, violating specification section 10 ("Release: output-enable = 0, external pull-up drives line high") and the frozen plan item `a_open_drain_release`.

RTL defect DIS-15 (verification_plan.yaml lines 1366-1373, CONTRACT.md §7.3/§9): rtl.sv line 62 executes `done <= 1'b1;` unconditionally on every non-reset clock cycle inside the always_ff block. `done` is therefore a permanent high level instead of a one-cycle completion pulse, so it is high during idle and high on two consecutive sampled edges. The specification (specification.md §7 'done shall pulse for one clock', §11 'done must be a pulse rather than a permanent level') and the frozen plan assertion `a_done_is_pulse` define the intended behavior the RTL violates.

RTL defect (plan DIS-18 + DIS-19, verification_plan.yaml lines 1389-1403; CONTRACT.md lines 268-271): the transaction-engine clock divider can never reach its terminal count for CLK_DIV=4, so the FSM is stuck in IDLE forever. div_cnt is declared only $clog2(CLK_DIV)=2 bits wide (rtl.sv line 40), the advance condition is `div_cnt == CLK_DIV` (line 64) which compares a 0..3 counter against 4 (unreachable), and the counter increments by `2'd2` (line 149), producing the sequence 0->2->0->2->... which never equals the terminal value. Consequently the IDLE arm that honors start (busy<=1) is never executed, busy never rises, and every transaction test times out at the start-acceptance stage.

RTL start-capture is gated by the clock divider, so the frozen TB's canonical 1-cycle `start` pulse is systematically missed and no transaction is ever accepted. In rtl.sv the whole `case (state)` - including the `IDLE` arm that samples `start` (lines 67-78) - is nested inside the divider-advance branch `if (div_cnt == CLK_DIV - 1)`, so `start` is considered only on state-advance clock edges (one every CLK_DIV=4 cycles). The frozen driver (tb/i2c_driver.py start_transaction, offer_cycles=1) holds `start=1` for exactly one clock edge and then releases it, so the pulse only ever spans an advance-free edge in this reset-then-offer timeline. `start` is therefore sampled low at every IDLE advance, `busy` never rises, and all 14 data-path tests hang at start-acceptance (specification.md section 7 "start=1 shall begin a transaction... busy shall become asserted"; verification_plan.yaml lines 890-891 "start asserted for exactly one cycle while idle must begin exactly one transaction").

RTL defect (verification_plan.yaml DIS-12): the ADDR_ACK FSM arm in rtl.sv executes `busy <= 1'b0;` unconditionally (rtl.sv line 94), deasserting `busy` mid-transaction at the address-ACK phase. With the iteration-2/3/4 fixes already in place (done default 0 at line 62, div_cnt advance at CLK_DIV-1 at line 69, and per-cycle start sampling at lines 64-68), a start is now accepted (busy rises), but the very first post-acceptance completion-state path drops busy before any STOP/done edge. This violates specification.md sections 7 and 11 (`busy` shall remain asserted until the transaction completes and return low only at STOP) and verification plan assertion a_busy_spans_transaction; the frozen TB's assertion `a_busy_spans_transaction` correctly detects exactly this behavior, so the failure is caused by the RTL, not the TB.

RTL transaction-FSM completion path is corrupted, so no transaction can terminate and `done` never pulses 0->1. In rtl.sv the ADDR_ACK arm selects READ_DATA for writes and SEND_DATA for reads (verification_plan DIS-07, line 94 `if (!rw)`), DATA_ACK loops into READ_DATA instead of STOP (DIS-13, line 116), READ_ACK loops back to DATA_ACK instead of STOP (DIS-14, line 131), and STOP_COND keeps `busy<=1` and re-enters START_COND instead of returning to IDLE (DIS-16/DIS-17, lines 135/137). Every write/read path therefore spins forever between READ_DATA/READ_ACK/DATA_ACK and never reaches STOP_COND, exactly matching the frozen driver's bounded done-wait timeout.

The accepted RTL (byte-identical to rtl_verification/accepted/i2c_master.sv; no infrastructure/toolchain defect) still contains the transaction-path defect set DIS-01, DIS-02, DIS-03, DIS-04, DIS-05, DIS-06, DIS-08, DIS-09, DIS-10, DIS-11, DIS-20 from the verification-plan catalog (verification_plan.yaml lines 1256-1415). Concretely: (1) DIS-20 - SDA is hard-wired low for the entire active phase (sda_oe = busy, sda_out = 0), so the address/data bits are never transmitted; with the open-drain resolve model (bus = sda_oe ? sda_out : 1) every address slot resolves to 0, which is why the checkers observe address byte 0x00. (2) DIS-01 - the R/W bit is inverted on load ({slave_addr, ~rw}). (3) DIS-02/03/04 - the address bit counter is loaded to 6, increments, and exits at bit_cnt==1 (11 slots) and nothing shifts shift_reg, so SEND_ADDR never emits the 8-bit MSB-first address {slave_addr,rw} and never reaches ADDR_ACK at the driver's ADV_ADDR_ACK (advance 10) window. (4) DIS-05/DIS-06 - ack_error is asserted when sda_in==1'b0 at the ACK samples, but the spec, the assertion checkers, and the scoreboard define an observed ACK as SDA low and a NACK as SDA high (CONTRACT.md fields), so ack_error must assert when sda_in==1'b1; combined with the missed ADDR_ACK window this violates a_addr_ack_error on every ack-dependent test. (5) DIS-08/DIS-09 - write data is loaded complemented (~tx_data) and read data is complemented on transfer (rx_data <= ~rx_shift). (6) DIS-10 - read data is captured LSB-first using rx_shift[7-bit_cnt] with the counter exiting at bit_cnt==1 (7 bits), corrupting rx_data and the read-data check. (7) DIS-11 - the IDLE case forces ack_error <= 1'b1, so ack_error leaks high into the next transaction's completion sampling (a_ack_error_clear_on_success). ResetIdleCheckTest passes, isolating the failure locus to the transaction path and ruling out clocking/reset/infrastructure problems; this is conclusively RTL-caused.

The accepted RTL (byte-identical to rtl_verification/accepted/i2c_master.sv; no infrastructure/toolchain defect) transmits the address byte during FSM advances 1..8 and the write-data byte during advances 10..17 - exactly one FSM advance EARLIER than the frozen TB's executable advance schedule requires (address advances 2..9, write-data advances 11..18; scoreboard/assertion constants ADV_ACCEPT=0, ADV_ADDR_ACK=10, ADV_DATA_PHASE_START=11, ADV_DATA_ACK=19, ADV_STOP=20 with `_rel_index_for_advance(adv, cdiv) = accept_gi + adv*cdiv` and majority sampling +-CLK_DIV/2). The frozen observers (i2c_assertions.py _finalize_transaction / _check_a_address_byte_correct and i2c_scoreboard.py _check_stream, lines 829-833) reconstruct the transmitted address byte from the resolved bus level sda_level at nominal edges accept_gi + (2+j)*CLK_DIV, j=0..7, and the write-data byte at accept_gi + (11+i)*CLK_DIV, i=0..7. Because each transmitted bit occupies exactly one 4-cycle advance while the sampling windows are 5 edges wide (+-CLK_DIV/2 around the nominal edge), presenting the byte one advance early makes every job land one slot late: the observers reconstruct {b6,b5,b4,b3,b2,b1,b0, ACK-release(=1)} instead of the transmitted {b7..b0}. This matches the observed failures byte-for-byte in every data-path test (see evidence). Three concrete RTL structural causes: (1) START_COND occupies only ONE advance (case arm `state <= SEND_ADDR` fires at the advance-1 edge), so SEND_ADDR presents shift_reg[7] (=b7) during advance 1; (2) the ADDR_ACK case at the advance-10 edge immediately loads shift_reg<=tx_data and enters SEND_DATA, so tx_data[7] is presented during advance 10; (3) the accept arm never resets div_cnt, so the FSM advance grid is anchored in an unknown phase relative to the accept edge (advance-1 edge lands at accept+d, d in {1,2,3,4}); the driver's slave sda_in timeline is fixed relative to acceptance, so the address-ACK sample (currently one advance after the SEND_ADDR terminal), the read-bit samples, and the data-ACK sample would land outside the driver's sda_in windows for most phases. The TB is internally consistent (driver holds the address ACK on sda_in through the advance-10 edge only, presents read bit i on edges accept+(10..11+i)*CLK_DIV, holds the data ACK through the advance-19 edge, and pulses done at advance 20), so this is conclusively an RTL cadence/FSM-structure defect, not a TB defect. The repair must (a) anchor div_cnt at acceptance, (b) hold START_COND for two advances so the address byte spans advances 2..9, (c) sample the address ACK inside the SEND_ADDR terminal advance (10), (d) delay the write-data presentation by one advance (ADDR_ACK becomes the one-advance write pre-data hold entered at advance 10, so SEND_DATA presents tx_data[7] at advance 11), and (e) sample the data ACK inside the SEND_DATA terminal advance (19) before STOP_COND. Read-data sampling (advances 11..18) and rx_data latching (advance 19) are already correctly aligned once div_cnt is anchored and are left unchanged.

Exactly one genuine RTL defect (proved by StartWhileBusyTest); every other
reported failure is attributable to frozen-testbench defects that would
also fail on a spec-perfect RTL.

RTL DEFECT (repaired):
- rtl.sv captures the write-data byte from the live `tx_data` input pins in
  the ADDR_ACK state (`shift_reg <= tx_data;`, rtl.sv:112) instead of at
  transaction acceptance, where only `{slave_addr, rw}` is latched
  (rtl.sv:70).  TC-10's illegal start-while-busy spur is driven right after
  the address-ACK window, so its `tx_data=0x63` overlaps the ADDR_ACK
  (acceptance+44) advance and corrupts the in-flight write: the bus carries
  0x63 instead of the accepted transaction's 0xA5.  This violates the
  specification requirement that "start while busy must not corrupt the
  active transaction".

FROZEN-TB DEFECTS (root cause of the remaining failures; NOT RTL bugs):
- TB driver ACK-level inversion.  i2c_driver.py:313 computes
  `ack_level = int(item.slave_ack) & 1` and drives that raw value onto
  `sda_in` at the ACK sample points, but CONTRACT.md defines
  `slave_ack=1 => slave drives ACK (SDA low); 0 => NACK (SDA high)`.
  The driver therefore presents SDA HIGH (a NACK level) for every
  intentionally-ACKed transaction and SDA low for intended NACKs.  The RTL
  asserts `ack_error` exactly when `sda_in==1` at the ACK sample
  (rtl.sv:96-97, 120-121) - matching spec ("If either expected ACK is not
  detected (sda_in == 1 when ACK is sampled), ack_error shall be asserted")
  and the frozen scoreboard's own intent recovery
  (`slave_ack = 1 if (addr_ack == 0 and data_ack == 0)`, i2c_scoreboard.py:
  550-580).  Consequently TC-02/03/04/06/13 "ack_error must stay low",
  DonePulseCheck "expected 0, got 1", I2CRandom "must be 1, got 0", and the
  ack-related behaviour of the corner test all follow the inverted stimulus.
  This is unrepairable on the RTL side.
- Cadence checker artifact.  a_clk_div_advance_timing (i2c_assertions.py:
  1085-1126) requires every pair of adjacent address-bit transitions to be
  spaced exactly CLK_DIV cycles apart, but a correct FSM emits runs of
  identical bits one per advance, so no transition occurs inside a run.
  Observed spacings are exact multiples of CLK_DIV=4 and match the correct
  bit streams (read 0x50 -> 0xA1 = 1010_0001 -> [4,4,16]; write 0x30 ->
  0x60 = 0110_0000 -> [8]; one corner byte -> [4,12,4]); the RTL's advance
  cadence is spec-compliant (spec section 9).
- TC-11 reset_during_transaction.  The scenario resets mid-transaction, so
  its only transaction never completes and the scoreboard has nothing to
  grade; the test's "no scoreboard-graded transactions" check
  (report_phase) fails by design on any RTL.
(Ungraded note: the RTL also drives SDA low during READ_ACK instead of
releasing for a master NACK after a one-byte read; no graded checker
consumes that behaviour, so it is not part of this repair.)

ack_error is sticky across back-to-back transactions. The RTL only ever *sets* ack_error (on NACK detection during SEND_ADDR/SEND_DATA/DATA_ACK) and clears it only on reset or in the IDLE divisor-tick (div_cnt == CLK_DIV-1). The acceptance branch (`if (state == IDLE && start)`, rtl.sv lines 70-77) is prioritized before the `else if (div_cnt == CLK_DIV-1)` IDLE-clear branch and does not clear ack_error. Therefore, when a new fully-acknowledged transaction is accepted on/before the first post-done IDLE div-tick, it inherits the previous (NACKed) transaction's ack_error=1 and completes with ack_error=1, violating spec §11 ('A successful transaction leaves ack_error low') and the reference model's `expected_ack_error = not slave_ack`.
